caption: The drawing depicts an ornately decorated architectural element, possibly a panel or a door, shown from both the front and side perspectives. The main section is vertically split into two parts: the left side is predominantly colored in shades of blue, while the right side is shaded in tones of red and light brown. Each side features a rectangular panel enclosed within a gold and green frame, and each panel contains a decorative motif including a red flower with green leaves and curling black flourishes. Surrounding the panels are gold circular ornaments aligned vertically. Along the top edge, there is a horizontal band with a sequence of circular designs in gold and green, supported by a cornice in light gray and orange hues. A horizontal board or molding, depicted in an orange-brown color, is placed at the very top. To the left, a vertical cross-section of the panel is drawn, revealing dimensional details and side profiles in grayscale. All components contain measurements in inches, annotated in black ink, and the drawing is executed with black ink outlines and colored washes. The drawing is signed and dated at the bottom right corner, with the scale indicated as 3 inches to 1 foot.
title: Pulpit - San Buenaventura Mission
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
